COMPLEX_FORAGER_STORAGE.source: Testart et al., The Significance of Food Storage Among Hunter-Gatherers (1982)
COMPLEX_FORAGER_STORAGE.use: predictable seasonal resources and storage can support higher density, sedentism and socioeconomic complexity without agriculture

FORAGING_NETWORKS.source: Hunter-gatherer foraging networks promote information transmission (2021)
FORAGING_NETWORKS.use: central-place foraging and intermediate mobility can increase network efficiency and information exchange

MESOLITHIC_MOBILITY_SEDENTISM_2025.source: Holst, Hunter-Gatherer Mobility and Sedentism, Oxford Handbook of Mesolithic Europe (2025)
MESOLITHIC_MOBILITY_SEDENTISM_2025.use: reduced residential mobility can coexist with individual mobility, managed territories, storage and long-distance exchange

R330_PARENT.source: R3.30 SEALED census-equivalent and weighted group ABM
R330_PARENT.use: census-equivalent, group counts, network counts, locations and organization modes are inherited authority

R331_PARENT.use: storage, transport/logistics, shelter/site engineering and specialization capacities are inherited authority

R332_PARENT.use: delayed-return economy, settlement commitment, regional continuity/differentiation and subsistence resilience are inherited authority

R336_PARENT.use: managed producer support, patch persistence and no-agriculture pathway are immutable parent authority

SOCIAL_NETWORK_MOBILITY.source: Social networks and information: Non-utilitarian mobility among hunter-gatherers (2006)
SOCIAL_NETWORK_MOBILITY.use: mobility maintains risk-buffering information and exchange networks, so settlement persistence does not imply network collapse

STORAGE_HUNTER_GATHERERS.source: Morgan, Caching your savings: small-scale storage in European prehistory (2011)
STORAGE_HUNTER_GATHERERS.use: storage is possible in mobile and semi-sedentary forager systems and must not be equated automatically with farming
